tests.name: test_counts_example
tests.description: For "the cat sat the cat ran", the table counts "cat" twice after "the".
tests.message: next_counts(['the', 'cat', 'sat', 'the', 'cat', 'ran']) is {'the': {'cat': 2}, 'cat': {'ran': 1}, 'sat': {'the': 1}}, not {'the': {'cat': 2}, 'cat': {'sat': 1, 'ran': 1}, 'sat': {'the': 1}}.

tests.name: test_counts_edges
tests.description: An empty list and a list of one word have no neighbouring pairs, so nothing follows anything.

tests.name: test_counts_add_up
tests.description: A list of n words has n - 1 neighbouring pairs, so the counts add up to n - 1.
tests.message: The counts of next_counts(['the', 'queen', 'and', 'the', 'king']) add up to 3, not 4.

tests.name: test_counts_join
tests.description: The table of two lists joined is the two tables added up, plus 1 for the pair where they meet.

tests.name: test_counts_leave_words
tests.description: next_counts leaves the list it is given as it was.

tests.name: test_most_likely
tests.description: After "said", Alice's counts give "the", 210 times in 462.

tests.name: test_ties
tests.description: A tie goes to the word first in alphabetical order, wherever it is in the dict.

tests.name: test_nothing_follows
tests.description: For a word that nothing follows, most_likely gives None.

tests.name: test_generate_puzzle
tests.description: With Alice's counts after "the", "queen" and "and", generate writes the puzzle's loop.

tests.name: test_generate_stops
tests.description: generate stops early at a word that nothing follows.

tests.name: test_generate_lengths
tests.description: generate gives exactly n words when it can, for n from 1 to 6.

tests.name: test_story
tests.description: The story in story.txt gives "the queen said nothing at all".
tests.message: generate(next_counts(words), 'the', 10) is ['the', 'cat', 'said', 'nothing', 'at', 'all'], not ['the', 'queen', 'said', 'nothing', 'at', 'all'].

tests.name: test_holds
tests.description: joins_right is True for pairs whose words join right.
tests.message: joins_right(letters_only, 'The cat', 'sat.') is False, not True: letters_only('The cat sat.') is ['the', 'cat', 'sat'], and letters_only('The cat') + letters_only('sat.') is ['the', 'cat', 'sat'].

tests.name: test_breaks
tests.description: joins_right is False when the join loses a word or changes one.
tests.message: joins_right(drops_last, 'ab', 'c') is True, not False: drops_last('ab c') is ['ab'], but drops_last('ab') + drops_last('c') is [].

tests.name: test_asks_for_the_joined_text
tests.description: joins_right asks the tokeniser it is given for the words of a + ' ' + b, of a and of b.
tests.message: joins_right(tokenise, 'ab', 'cd') never asked tokenise for the words of 'ab cd'; it asked for ['abcd', 'ab', 'cd'].

tests.name: test_shrink_a
tests.description: For a tokeniser that loses a word at the end, ('ab cd', 'ef') shrinks to ('d', ''): a first, then b.
tests.message: shrink_pair(drops_last, 'ab cd', 'ef') is ('ab cd', 'ef'), not ('d', ''). Take the characters of a out from the first: when a removal is kept, the next character moves into its place, so try that place again, and move on only when the removal mends the property.

tests.name: test_shrink_b
tests.description: For a tokeniser that skips the first character, ('xy', 'ab') shrinks to ('', 'b').
tests.message: shrink_pair(skips_first, 'xy', 'ab') is ('y', 'b'), not ('', 'b').

tests.name: test_shrink_apostrophe
tests.description: For a tokeniser that looks back past the start, ('x', "'ab") shrinks to ('', "'b").
tests.message: shrink_pair(looks_back, 'x', "'ab") is ('x', 'b'), not ('', "'b").

tests.name: test_shrink_small_pair
tests.description: A pair that is already as small as it can be stays as it is.

tests.name: test_first_pair
tests.description: find_bug gives the first pair that breaks the property, shrunk, after making just the texts up to it, a and then b.
tests.message: With the texts 'ab ', 'c', 'd', 'e f' and so on, find_bug(drops_last, make, 3) is ('d', ' '), not ('d', ''): the first pair is ('ab ', 'c'), which keeps the property, and the second, ('d', 'e f'), breaks it and shrinks to ('d', '').

tests.name: test_none
tests.description: find_bug gives None when every pair keeps the property, after making 2 texts for each trial.
tests.message: find_bug(letters_only, make, 50) is ('b', 'c'), not None, though every pair keeps the property.

tests.name: test_random_texts
tests.description: With random texts, it gives None for two wrong tokenisers that keep the property, and a pair for three that break it.
tests.message: find_bug(letters_only, random_text, 300) is ('न', 'न'), not None.

tests.name: test_example
tests.description: The Explore phase's text gives its six words, with "the" and "cat" twice.

tests.name: test_empty_and_one_word
tests.description: An empty text has no words, and a text of one word has just that word, in lower case.

tests.name: test_apostrophe_inside
tests.description: An apostrophe between two letters stays in its word.
tests.message: tokens("Don't panic, it's five o'clock: rock'n'roll.") is ['don', 't', 'panic', 'it', 's', 'five', 'o', 'clock', 'rock', 'n', 'roll'], not ["don't", 'panic', "it's", 'five', "o'clock", "rock'n'roll"].

tests.name: test_quotation_marks
tests.description: An apostrophe at the start or the end of a word is a quotation mark, and is left out.

tests.name: test_apostrophe_last
tests.description: An apostrophe that is the last character of the text is left out, without looking past the end.
tests.message: tokens("don't'") is ['don', 't'], not ["don't"].

tests.name: test_hindi
tests.description: A word of Hindi keeps its vowel signs and the sign that joins two consonants, which are marks.
tests.message: tokens('नमस्ते') is ['नमस', 'त'], not ['नमस्ते'].

tests.name: test_tamil
tests.description: Words of Tamil, with their marks, are whole words.
tests.message: tokens('வணக்கம், தமிழ்') is ['வணக', 'கம', 'தம', 'ழ'], not ['வணக்கம்', 'தமிழ்'].

tests.name: test_digits
tests.description: Digits, in any script, belong to words: an apostrophe between digits stays, and a full stop between digits ends a word.
tests.message: tokens('Chapter 12') is ['chapter'], not ['chapter', '12'].

tests.name: test_capitals
tests.description: Capital letters become small ones, accented ones too.

tests.name: test_separate_accent
tests.description: An accent typed as a mark after its letter, U+0301, stays in the word.
tests.message: tokens('café au lait') is ['cafe', 'au', 'lait'], not ['café', 'au', 'lait']: the accent, U+0301, is a mark and should stay in its word.

tests.name: test_example
tests.description: 'It was late. She ran.' has 2 sentences.
tests.message: count_sentences('It was late. She ran.') is 1, not 2.

tests.name: test_empty_and_one_word
tests.description: An empty text has no sentences, and nor has a text of one word with no full stop, ! or ? after it.

tests.name: test_not_followed_by_space
tests.description: A full stop, ! or ? followed by a letter, a digit or another of them ends nothing.
tests.message: count_sentences('It cost 3.50 rupees.') is 0, not 1.

tests.name: test_quotation_mark
tests.description: A full stop, ! or ? followed by a closing quotation mark ends a sentence.

tests.name: test_whitespace
tests.description: A full stop, ! or ? followed by a newline or a tab ends a sentence, as one followed by a space does.
tests.message: count_sentences('One.\nTwo.') is 1, not 2.

tests.name: test_the_rule
tests.description: The rule counts the full stop of Mr. too, so the Explore phase's text gives 3.
tests.message: count_sentences('Mr. Brown paid 3.50 rupees. Was it worth it?!') is 2, not 3, which is what the rule gives.

tests.name: test_join
tests.description: The sentence counts of two texts joined with a space add up.
tests.message: count_sentences('Hi. Yo.') is 1, but count_sentences('Hi.') + count_sentences('Yo.') is 0: the counts of two texts joined with a space should add up.

tests.name: test_end_of_the_text
tests.description: A full stop, ! or ? that is the last character of the text ends a sentence.
tests.message: count_sentences('Hi!') is 0, not 1.
